items.title: Water Minute · What hard water is doing to your skin
items.preview:
Words I like;
Clean water shouldn't cost you comfort.
Ever step out of the shower and your skin feels tight, like it shrunk a size? Maybe the kids scratch at dry patches, or the eczema flares up and won't quit. A lot of folks blame their soap. Usually it's the water.
Here's what's happening. Hard water is loaded with calcium and magnesium. When that mineral meets your soap, it doesn't rinse clean. It forms a sticky film, the same scummy ring you see in the tub, and it sits right on your skin. That film traps dirt, clogs pores, and strips the natural oils your skin uses to hold moisture.
For most people that means dryness and itch. For anyone with eczema or sensitive skin, it's worse. The minerals keep the skin barrier irritated, so flare-ups stick around longer than they should.
Soften that water and the soap finally rinses away. No film, no scum, oils stay put. Skin calms down.
If you already own one of our systems, this is a big reason you stopped fighting dry skin. Good call.
Curious what's in your water? Reply and I'll send you our free water assessment.
As promised, value in under a minute.
Justin
CEO / ClearWave

items.title: Email Campaign · : Referral Push (30-60 Day Post-Install)
items.preview:
**Rationale:** This is the highest-conversion play available. These clients are freshly satisfied (30-60 days in, system is new and impressing them), and the referral bonus is concrete cash. No HARD RULE conflicts (referrals are explicitly encouraged, review asks are banned). Much higher intent than cold leads.
### 1. Campaign name + audience size
**"Fresh Water, Found Money"**. Referral push segment, **30 contacts**
### 2. Subject line + alternates (all under 60 char, no dashes)
- **Primary (specific):** `$500 for every neighbor who tastes the difference`
- (curiosity): `The thing people ask you about now`
- (pain): `Your friends are still drinking that?`
- (authority): `A quiet favor from ClearWave`
- (specific): `How your water turns into $500`
### 3. Preview text (under 90 char)
`A few weeks in, people start noticing. Here is what that is worth to you.`
### 4. Email body
Hi Sarah,
It's been about two months since we installed your ClearWave system, and if you're like most of our clients, people have started to notice. The coffee. The shower. The way the water just tastes like nothing (in the best way).
So here's the simple part. When someone asks, send them our way for a free water assessment. If they become a client, you get $500 cash. Refer more and it grows: $750 for your sixth through ninth, and $1,000 each once you hit ten in a year. Even if they just book the assessment and don't move forward, we send you a $50 gift card for the introduction.
No pressure, no selling on your end. Just point them to us and we handle the rest.
Reply to this email with a name, or forward it along.
Justin
CEO / ClearWave
### 5. Send timing
**Tuesday, 10:00 AM ET** (mid-morning weekday, strong B2C open window; avoids Monday inbox clearing).
### 6. Expected performance
- **Open: 48-55%** (above your 42.3% baseline; small, warm, recently-engaged segment + curiosity/specific subject).
- **Click/reply: 3-6%** (your campaign history shows ~0.28% click, but those were broadcast blasts to 3,687 with weak CTAs. This is a 30-person warm segment with a cash offer and a reply-based CTA, which dramatically outperforms link clicks).
- **Conversion (named referral): 2-4 introductions.** Even one closed referral = $500 payout against near-zero send cost.
### 7. Source justification
Draws from **Jobber Lifecycle Triggers → Referral push candidates (30-60 days post-install, satisfied)** and the **Referral Bonus Structure** block. Honors HARD RULE #2 (blanket tenure line, no legacy "H2O Protector" name), #3 (referral not review), #3a ("free water assessment").

items.title: Email Campaign · : Concierge "Is It Worth It?" Upsell
items.preview:
**Rationale:** Largest qualified list (100), all past their year-1 service (so HARD RULE #1 is satisfied: these are 13-24 months post-install), and $99/mo recurring revenue is high LTV. The "here's the math" framing matches your prescribed non-pushy voice.
### 1. Campaign name + audience size
**"The Year 1.5 Question"**. Concierge upsell candidates, **100 contacts**
### 2. Subject line + alternates (all under 60 char, no dashes)
- **Primary (curiosity):** `The question we get at the 18 month mark`
- (specific): `Is $99 a month actually worth it? The math.`
- (pain): `Who swaps your filters now?`
- (authority): `What a ClearWave Concierge actually covers`
- (specific): `Annual service, filters, parts: one number`
### 3. Preview text (under 90 char)
`Not a pitch. Just the honest math on whether Concierge makes sense for you.`
### 4. Email body
Hi John,
It's been a little over a year since we installed your ClearWave system, which means you've had your first annual service and you know how we work.
Right around this point we get the same question: "Is the Concierge thing actually worth it for me?" Fair question. Here's the honest math.
Concierge is $99 a month. It covers your annual service, filter swaps, priority phone support, and parts on your standard install components. If you're currently handling service and filters as you go, this usually comes out even or ahead, with the bonus that you never have to think about scheduling or tracking a replacement cycle again. We just handle it.
If you'd rather stay pay-as-you-go, that's completely fine. Your system is built to run clean either way. But if "set it and forget it" sounds good, reply and I'll get you set up.
Justin
CEO / ClearWave
### 5. Send timing
**Thursday, 11:00 AM ET** (gives Proposal 1 its own send day; Thursday late-morning performs well for considered B2C decisions).
### 6. Expected performance
- **Open: 44-50%** (near baseline; "question we get" curiosity hook on a warm, trusting segment).
- **Click/reply: 1-3%** (reply-based, concrete $99 value math; recurring-revenue asks convert lower than cash giveaways but the audience is 3x larger).
- **Conversion: 2-5 enrollments.** At $99/mo, even 3 enrollments = ~$3,500/yr recurring from one send.
### 7. Source justification
Draws from **Jobber Lifecycle Triggers → Concierge upsell candidates (13-24 months, not on Concierge)** and the **Concierge Upsell Context** block (pricing, "is it worth it" framing, non-pushy voice). Honors HARD RULE #1 (list pre-filtered to 13+ months, all past year-1 service), #2 (tenure line for "Reionator Pro Ultra" legacy name), #4/#5 (sign-off, no dashes).
---
**Why these two over the alternatives:** The 1-year annual service list (23) is a service reminder, not a high-conversion marketing campaign, and it borders on the Concierge timing floor. The cold lead re-engagement (1,000) is valuable but lower per-contact conversion and better run as a standalone nurture after these two warm, high-intent plays. I'd recommend queuing the cold re-engagement for next week.
